s: User registration: creates account via POST /api/users, automatically logs in after success, stores JWT in Redux + localStorage.
Registration depends on User model, bcrypt password hashing, and generateToken; new users get isAdmin=false by default.
User logout: clears userInfo from localStorage and dispatches USER_LOGOUT to reset all Redux state slices.
Profile view and update: authenticated users edit name, email, and password on ProfileScreen, saved via PUT /api/users/profile.
Profile edge cases: empty password field skips update, token refreshes after profile change, concurrent order list loading.
JWT infrastructure: generateToken signs user ID and isAdmin into 30-day token, protect middleware verifies Bearer token on each request.
JWT depends on JWT_SECRET env var and User model; all protected features depend on this authentication mechanism.
Add to cart: ProductScreen navigates to /cart/:id?qty=N, CartScreen dispatches addToCart action, saves to localStorage.
CartScreen displays items with quantity dropdowns, delete buttons, and order summary card with subtotal and checkout button.
Remove from cart: trash icon dispatches CART_REMOVE_ITEM filtering out the product, updates localStorage cartItems.
Cart persistence: cartItems stored in localStorage, loaded as initial Redux state on page refresh via store.js.
Cart summary card: auto-calculated subtotal (sum of price × qty), item count, and checkout button redirecting to login.
Product listing: HomeScreen displays paginated product grid with keyword search, top-rated carousel, and responsive columns.
Product detail: ProductScreen shows product image, metadata, price, quantity selector, add-to-cart button, and review section.
Product search: keyword parameter filters products via MongoDB regex on name field, with paginated results.
Product carousel: displays top-rated products on homepage via GET /api/products/top endpoint, hidden during search.
Product reviews: authenticated users submit 1-5 star rating + comment, one review per user, creates Review sub-document.
CheckoutSteps component: 4-step progress indicator showing Sign In → Shipping → Payment → Place Order with active/disabled states.
Shipping screen: address/city/postal code/country form, saves to Redux cart.shippingAddress and localStorage.
Payment screen: radio button for PayPal/credit card, saves paymentMethod to Redux cart state and proceeds to order review.
Place order screen: review of shipping, payment, and items with auto-calculated prices, submits via POST /api/orders.
Order details screen: shows complete order with PayPal payment button for unpaid orders, mark-as-delivered for admin on paid orders.
PayPal SDK dynamic loading: fetches client ID from server, creates script tag, sets sdkReady state for button rendering.
PayPal payment flow: onApprove callback sends PayPal order ID to backend, marks order paid with payment result and timestamp.

Incident i-001: PayPal sandbox fired onApprove twice causing double payment marking and inventory decrement; fixed with idempotency check.
Timeline of PayPal double-charge: sandbox retry fired second onApprove 2s later, stock decremented twice, caught by QA next day.
Root cause: PayPal sandbox non-standard double-firing of onApprove callback; fix adds idempotency check before payment processing.
Resolution: added idempotency gate checking existing paymentResult before processing, verified with load test of 50 rapid callbacks.
Incident i-002: MongoDB connection pool exhaustion during Black Friday 2023 caused 2h43m complete outage from default 5-connection limit.
Black Friday timeline: request rate 8→180 req/min, pool hit ceiling at 5 connections, errors started at 08:43, 50% error rate by 08:47.
Root cause: Mongoose default maxPoolSize of 5 insufficient for 180 req/min traffic, requests queued indefinitely causing MongoTimeoutError.
Resolution: increased maxPoolSize to 25, added connection pool monitoring, upgraded Atlas to M10 for higher connection limits.
Incident i-003: .env file with JWT secret and MongoDB credentials committed to git in Feb 2023, discovered 17 months later in security audit.
Timeline: .env committed Feb 2023, removed from working dir but not git history, discovered Jul 2024 during open-source preparation audit.
Root cause: .gitignore didn't include .env file, no pre-commit secret scanning, .env removed from working dir but persisted in git history.
Resolution: rotated all secrets (JWT, MongoDB, PayPal), rewrote git history with git-filter-repo, invalidated all active JWT sessions.

A/B testing runbook: designing experiments with clear hypothesis, sample size calculation, test duration, and success criteria.
A/B test basics: Control vs Variant split, measuring conversion rate, average order value, and cart abandonment rate.
Pre-test checklist: clear hypothesis, defined metrics, calculated sample size, decided test duration, set success criteria.
Sample size calculation: determines minimum users per variant for statistically significant results based on expected effect size.
Test execution: random variant assignment via feature flags, 50/50 traffic split, event tracking for both variants.
Results analysis: calculate p-value, check statistical significance (p<0.05), measure lift, declare winner or inconclusive.
A/B test pitfalls: peeking at results early, running multiple comparisons, Simpson's paradox, and insufficient sample sizes.
ProShop example: A/B test design for multi_step_checkout_v2 with 50/50 split measuring conversion rate lift.
Test documentation template for recording hypothesis, methodology, results, and decision from A/B experiments.
Incident response runbook: severity classification P0-P3, structured phases from discovery through postmortem review.
Severity levels: P0 immediate response (complete outage), P1 under 15 min (significant degradation), P2 under 1 hour, P3 no urgency.
Incident phases: discovery → declaration → triage → mitigation → resolution → verification → postmortem.
Incident communication: regular status updates, dedicated Slack channel, stakeholder notification at each phase transition.
Postmortem process: blameless review, root cause analysis, timeline reconstruction, action items with owners and deadlines.
ProShop-specific incident response procedures tailored to the MERN stack deployment on Render.com with MongoDB Atlas.
Deployment runbook: pre-deployment checklist, environment variables setup, Heroku deployment steps, rollback procedures.
Pre-deployment checklist: all tests pass, code reviewed and merged, env vars verified, database backup taken, rollback plan documented.
Production environment setup: NODE_ENV=production, Atlas connection string, strong JWT secret, production PayPal client ID.
Deploy steps: push to Heroku, heroku-postbuild builds frontend, Express serves static build, verify deployment health.
Rollback procedure: Heroku rollback to previous release, database migration rollback if schema changed, verify service health.
Local setup runbook: step-by-step guide for bootstrapping ProShop on a fresh machine in 10-15 minutes.
Prerequisites: Node.js v14+, npm v6+, Docker Desktop for MongoDB, git, and a text editor or IDE.
